title: Figure 34 - Modelled supply generation, demand profiles, and expected unserved energy over a two-day period capturing an unserved energy event, including the preceding day in 2026-27 (sample day in March 2027, reference year 2017-18) (MW)
notes: All 97 half-hour samples are retained, including the endpoint of the two-day period. Dates and times are decoded directly from the worksheet's Excel serial values.

Generation, distributed PV, available headroom and outages are stacked above zero as in the original. Charging is shown below zero; its source values are positive and are sign-inverted only for display.
ESR state of charge uses the right-hand percentage axis, aligned at zero with the MW axis. Demand uses the left-hand MW axis.

DSP includes those with assigned Capacity Credit or NCESS contract, making them available during their obligation periods. In 2026-27, March 21 falls on a Sunday, so no DSP with Capacity Credit is required to be available that day.

Report context: the first day has generation headroom and batteries charge ahead of the event. On the second evening headroom is exhausted, DSP is unavailable on Sunday, and battery injection is insufficient to avoid unserved energy.
